cards.title: Flawed Study Shaped Childhood Depression Treatment
cards.body: A single flawed study influenced clinical guidance for prescribing Prozac to children with depression. Science is self-correcting, and this error highlights the importance of rigorous research in pediatric mental health.

cards.title: Benefits of Having an Older Sibling
cards.body: Older siblings influence younger siblings in ways parents often cannot, serving as trusted role models and mentors. This dynamic proves especially valuable during the challenging adolescent years.

cards.title: When Infants Cry Excessively Support Parents Too
cards.body: When babies cry excessively, parents often struggle with stress and emotional exhaustion. New research highlights that parent-focused support is just as important as addressing the infant's needs.

cards.title: Understanding the Gut-Brain Axis in Children
cards.body: A flood in Walkerton, Canada led to hundreds of cases of IBS and associated depression, documenting the gut-brain connection. Grandmothers who sent children to pick field greens knew this instinctively—science now confirms it.

cards.title: Why Winnie the Pooh Endures for Generations
cards.body: Over 100 years later, Winnie the Pooh remains as popular with children as ever. Its timeless appeal offers insights into child development and what stories mean to growing minds.
